verses.english: Numbered Discourses 8.35
4. Giving
Rebirth by Giving
“Mendicants, there are these eight rebirths by giving.
What eight?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco dānaṁ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
verses.english: First, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.
Whatever they give they expect back.

verses.pali: So passati khattiyamahāsāle vā brāhmaṇamahāsāle vā gahapatimahāsāle vā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappite samaṅgībhūte paricārayamāne.
verses.english: They see a well-to-do aristocrat or brahmin or householder amusing themselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.
It occurs to them:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā khattiyamahāsālānaṁ vā brāhmaṇamahāsālānaṁ vā gahapatimahāsālānaṁ vā sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of well-to-do aristocrats or brahmins or householders!’

verses.pali: So taṁ cittaṁ dahati, taṁ cittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, taṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ hīne vimuttaṁ, uttari abhāvitaṁ, tatrūpapattiyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

verses.pali: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā khattiyamahāsālānaṁ vā brāhmaṇamahāsālānaṁ vā gahapatimahāsālānaṁ vā sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of well-to-do aristocrats or brahmins or householders.

verses.pali: Tañca kho sīlavato vadāmi, no dussīlassa.
verses.english: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.
The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

verses.pali: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco dānaṁ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
verses.english: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins …
Whatever they give they expect back.
And they’ve heard:
‘The gods of the four great kings are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’
It occurs to them:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings!’ …

verses.pali: So taṁ cittaṁ dahati, taṁ cittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, taṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
Tassa taṁ cittaṁ hīne vimuttaṁ, uttari abhāvitaṁ, tatrūpapattiyā saṁvattati.
Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings.

verses.pali: Tañca kho sīlavato vadāmi, no dussīlassa.
verses.english: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.
The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

verses.pali: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco dānaṁ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
verses.english: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins …
Whatever they give they expect back.
And they’ve heard:
‘The gods of the thirty-three …’
‘The gods of Yama …’
‘The joyful gods …’
‘The gods who love to create …’
‘The gods who control what is created by others are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’
It occurs to them:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others!’

verses.pali: So taṁ cittaṁ dahati, taṁ cittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, taṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ hīne vimuttaṁ, uttari abhāvitaṁ, tatrūpapattiyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

verses.pali: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others.

verses.pali: Tañca kho sīlavato vadāmi, no dussīlassa.
verses.english: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.
The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

verses.pali: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco dānaṁ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
verses.english: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.
Whatever they give they expect back.
And they’ve heard:
‘The gods of the Divinity’s host are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’
It occurs to them:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā brahmakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host!’

verses.pali: So taṁ cittaṁ dahati, taṁ cittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, taṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ hīne vimuttaṁ, uttari abhāvitaṁ, tatrūpapattiyā saṁvattati.
verses.english: As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

verses.pali: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā brahmakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host.

verses.pali: Tañca kho sīlavato vadāmi, no dussīlassa;
verses.english: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.
And for those free of desire, not those with desire.
The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their freedom from desire.
These are the eight rebirths by giving.”
